mutations.name: a-silent-arm-reads-as-same
mutations._mechanism: The defect the whole tool exists to prevent: two arms that observed nothing compare equal, and `SAME` is the most believable lie available — it reads as a real finding about the variable.

mutations.name: an-empty-log-counts-as-an-observation
mutations._mechanism: Exit 0 with an empty log is exactly the shape of a dispatch killed by its parent shell — the failure this repo spent a session misreading as `agy is down`.

mutations.name: a-non-matching-log-counts-as-an-observation
mutations._mechanism: A log that ran and says nothing about the observable is evidence the probe was aimed wrong, not evidence of sameness. Re-anchored when J39 rewrote this line from first-match to last-match — the drift the harness caught rather than a reviewer, and the reason `--check-anchors` runs before every mutation run.
mutations.find: return matches[-1].group(1) if matches else None

mutations.name: the-control-check-is-skipped
mutations._mechanism: An uncontrolled pair runs to completion, the numbers differ, and the difference is attributed to the wrong cause. The run looks exactly like a successful experiment.

mutations.name: a-value-may-smuggle-the-placeholder
mutations._mechanism: A value containing {{VAR}} re-expands, so the arms differ in more than the declared variable while still looking like a single-variable diff.
mutations.find: if placeholder in value_a or placeholder in value_b:

mutations.name: two-identical-values-are-a-valid-experiment
mutations._mechanism: Nothing varies, so any observed difference is noise between two runs of the same prompt — and it would be recorded as the variable's effect.

mutations.name: a-missing-placeholder-is-fine
mutations._mechanism: Both arms are then byte-identical; the tool would report DIFFERENT on run-to-run variation alone.

mutations.name: the-exit-code-decides-the-verdict
mutations._mechanism: The one surface that must never carry the finding. A killed dispatch, a skipped test and a clean run all exit 0, and this repo has been fooled by each of the three. The discriminating direction is observations EQUAL with exits DIFFERENT: a test where BOTH differ passes under the mutant, and named it a survivor.

mutations.name: the-crashed-arm-is-hidden
mutations._mechanism: The exit code is not scored, but it must still be reported: an arm that crashed and happened to differ would otherwise read as a clean result.

mutations.name: the-prompts-are-not-written
mutations._mechanism: An A/B nobody can re-read afterwards is an anecdote, and the arms are exactly what a reader needs to check the control claim independently.

mutations.name: an-observe-without-a-capture-group-is-accepted
mutations._mechanism: `match.group(1)` then raises AFTER both dispatches have been paid for — the most expensive possible moment to discover a typo in the probe.

mutations.name: the-cli-exits-0-on-inconclusive
mutations._mechanism: A caller reading `$?` cannot tell an experiment that measured nothing from one that measured a difference.

mutations.name: both-arms-get-the-same-value
mutations._mechanism: Silent collapse to a single-arm run wearing an experiment's report.

mutations.name: observe-takes-the-prompt-echo
mutations._mechanism: J39 restored. An agent's log carries the PROMPT before the answer, so first-match returns the observable's own name quoted out of the instruction. Both arms echo the same prompt, so both observe the same value and the run reports SAME -- 'the rule is present and not causally effective'. That is a FINDING, not an error, which is why nothing downstream can catch it: the tool built to establish causality reports the prompt back as its result.
mutations.find: return matches[-1].group(1) if matches else None
mutations.replace: return matches[0].group(1) if matches else None

mutations.name: an-unobserved-arm-returns-empty-instead-of-none
mutations._mechanism: `None` is what drives INCONCLUSIVE. Return `""` and two silent arms compare EQUAL, so a run that observed nothing reports SAME -- the exact lie the verdict set was designed around, reached through the observer instead of the comparator. Pinned to the BLANK-log test on purpose: this branch is the empty log, not the non-matching one, and the harness caught the mis-attribution by reporting the mutant as killed by the wrong assertion while its named test passed.

mutations.name: run-token-parsing-reverts-to-argparse
mutations._mechanism: J38 restored. argparse reads any value beginning with '-' as an option, so the space-separated form SKILL.md documents dies with `expected one argument` -- for every real dispatch argv, since they all start with flags. The tool is then broken precisely as documented, which is the shape that survives longest.

mutations.name: both-arms-share-every-other-path
mutations._mechanism: J40/F5 restored. Without {arm}, every per-arm path the operator passes beyond {prompt}/{log} is byte-identical across arms: arm B overwrites arm A and the comparison reads B against B. It reports SAME -- 'the rule is not causally effective' -- which is the most believable wrong answer this tool can produce and the one its verdict set exists to prevent.
